swept: A node scan of all 33 wines (every sale and every staged description) through the engine's words() and sentences() (sale two sentences, 15 to 45 words; description 104 to 110), the dish link rule (every printed dish name matched against the wine's derived firstPickIds, secondFor and offeredWith, and every tier word beside it), the step (by the glass, Coravin, half bottle, magnum against the record), BANNED_WORDS, superlatives (best, finest, greatest, most, top, legendary, iconic, world class, every -est word, than any), hedges, prices, questions, allergens, dashes, American spellings from the engine's own list, provenance, living names (the engine's living list, printed names exempt), every proper name and year against the hay and the house (sourceProblems), the eight word run against the s20 and the description's opening on the printed name. Found: three superlatives (Montelena came top, twice; Kongsgaard top bottling) and one tier misreading (Réserve Personnelle, a classic of Alsace beside a celebration bottle), all fixed; the other hits were flavour words (baked apple, the creamed spinach of the linked Eggs Sardou), the printed estate name Stein and plain facts (one of the nine estates), left as they stand.
